title: Bounded-time loop evaluation
statement: Let $M$ be a Boolean Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, let $C_j$ be configurations on a fixed input indexed by natural numbers, and let $P(j)$ be a Boolean predicate. Suppose that at index $N$, $C_N$ is halted with output the one-element word $[\mathrm{false}]$. Also suppose that for every $j<N$ there is a time $t\le B$ such that, if $P(j)$ holds, the run from $C_j$ halts with output $[\mathrm{true}]$ after $t$ steps; if $P(j)$ does not hold, that run reaches $C_{j+1}$ after $t$ steps. Then the run from $C_0$ halts within $N B$ steps with output the one-element word whose bit is true exactly when $P(j)$ holds for some $j<N$.
hypotheses_covered: Boolean Turing machine with $k$ work tapes
configuration sequence $C_j$ on a fixed input
for every $j<N$, there is a time $t\le B$ satisfying the stated conditional run outcome
